described.alt_text: A photograph beneath the BQE overpass at Columbia Street with a graffiti mural, where a tall pink signal box has grown horns and a tail, a traffic pole wears a purple creature's body, and the sidewalk is bleached tan, signed 24.
described.description: A portrait format digital piece on a photograph, signed Matt Crump 24 at lower right. A green steel overpass crosses the top with a cream concrete wall at left carrying blue stencil faces and tags. A wall beneath the overpass carries a real colourful graffiti mural with a white arrow drawn pointing at it, and a street sign reads Columbia St. In the foreground a tall salmon pink signal box is redrawn as a creature with white horns, a round white eye, a pink slot mouth and a curling tail at its base. At right a traffic signal pole is drawn with its signals as teal and yellow cartoon boxes and a purple rounded body with feet at its base, with cartoon street signs on the pole. Small tufts of drawn grass sprout from the kerb, and a cartoon figure stands under the overpass in the distance. The sidewalk and road are bleached warm tan and the shadows are flat.
described.impression: Street furniture waking up: the signal box has become a tall shy monster and the traffic pole has grown a purple body. The arrow pointing at the real graffiti is the drawing acknowledging its ancestor. Under the highway on a hot afternoon, with nothing much happening and everything slightly alive.
